tagline: Fifteen miles of dirt along the rim of Linville Gorge.
intro: The loop starts nine miles northwest of Morganton and climbs NC 181 into the Pisgah National Forest, with Table Rock and Hawksbill in view, past a rare mountain wetland to Jonas Ridge. Beyond the Linville Falls trailhead the pavement ends. For about fifteen miles Old NC 105 runs unpaved with the Linville Gorge Wilderness on its east side, then comes down to cross the Linville River where it runs into Lake James.
The gorge is about 1,400 feet deep and so steep that no industrial logging ever took place in it, and much of its forest is old growth. The Cherokee called the river Ee-see-oh, river of many cliffs.

moments.title: Table Rock
moments.text: The distinctive rock on the gorge's east rim turned up in Jules Verne's 1904 novel Master of the World as the Great Eyrie, belching strange sounds and fire over Morganton.

moments.title: Wiseman's View
moments.text: A short, accessible trail ends at an overlook on Table Rock, Hawksbill Mountain and the Chimneys, with the Linville River running through the gorge far below.

moments.title: Lake James
moments.text: The river leaves the gorge here for Lake James, and the Linville access area on its shore is where the fort battle and canoe scenes of The Last of the Mohicans were filmed.

practical: About 15 miles of Old NC 105 along Linville Gorge are mostly unpaved, and four-wheel drive is required there. Tractor-trailers are prohibited and the route is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses. The guidebook gives a paved alternative by US 221 and Lake James Road.
